text:
PagerDuty Bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: SEV2 - network egress degradation detected in eu-central (service=redwood-egress). Multiple customers reporting increased latency and DNS failures. Alert group: net-egress-eu-central.
Maya Chen: I’m on it. grabbing dashboards now. which peers are impacted?
NetOps Bot: Alert snapshot: 60s spike in packet loss to 35% for routes via AS27678 (provider 'CarrierZ') across eu-central egress. BGP flap count = 18 in last 10m. Link: https://grafana.internal/d/egress/eu-central?panel=5
Ajay Patel: I can reproduce from my laptop — curl to api.redwood.com -> lots of RTOs. traceroute shows turnover between AS27678 and AS64512.
Ajay Patel: paste:```
traceroute to 52.23.12.34 (52.23.12.34), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.0.1  0.64 ms
 2  198.51.100.1  2.1 ms
 3  * * *
 4  203.0.113.5  80.2 ms  AS27678
 5  203.0.113.9  81.0 ms  AS27678 -> AS64512 flap
 6  52.23.12.34  82.3 ms
```
Sarah Gomez: DNS checks: resolver-paths from eu-central show inconsistent AS paths for our authoritative edge; some queries hit alternate POP with much higher latency.
Maya Chen: Ok - sounds like CarrierZ is oscillating on some transit links causing path churn and impacting DNS as well. Declaring SEV2. Opening incident channel and tagging cs.
Emily (Customer Success): Noted. I’ll prep a customer-facing blurb — need ETA or mitigation plan first.
Maya Chen: Initial mitigation plan: 1) attempt traffic steering away from CarrierZ by withdrawing selective prefixes to that peer and re-advertising via AlternatePeer (AS65001) 2) ask CarrierZ for community-based dampening or to check their upstream flapping 3) increase DNS replication TTLs temporarily and move critical zones to alternate authoritative nodes.
Leo Anders: Paging network oncall to run show bgp summary on core. /me taking over console.
NetOps Bot: runbook: net/egress/bgp-churn - recommended immediate actions: set local-pref higher for PreferredPeer, send AS_PATH prepend to CarrierZ to reduce preference, and throttle BGP timers if supported.
Leo Anders: Doing quick check:```
show bgp summary | include 27678
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcvd MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
203.0.113.5     4 27678   12345  12350  987654     0    0 00:12:34  240
```
Leo Anders: Pfx flaps seen on ~240 prefixes via CarrierZ. I’m going to coordinate with infra to withdraw non-critical less-specific prefixes from that peer to force reroute.
Ajay Patel: If we withdraw, watch for traffic surge on AlternatePeer — check capacity. Can we do weighted localpref instead of full withdraw?
Maya Chen: Good point. Start with local-pref bump for AlternatePeer (+100) for critical egress ranges (52.0.0.0/16 + 34.0.0.0/16), leave others for gradual steering.
Sarah Gomez: DNS plan: switching primary NS for prod zones to alt-authoritative in eu-central2. TTL bump to 60s -> 300s for critical records. Will do a staged rollover.
NetOps Bot: Note: change window will propagate ~TTL seconds; monitor for DNS cache inconsistencies.
Maya Chen: Ajay/Leo, make the BGP localpref change and observe. Post commands you run.
Leo Anders: Running config change now.```
configure terminal
router bgp 64496
  neighbor 198.51.100.2 route-map PREFER-ALT in
exit
write memory
```
Leo Anders: Applied PREFER-ALT route-map (localpref +100) for AlternatePeer. Watching routing table...
NetOps Bot: Route table delta: 52/32 prefixes switched to AlternatePeer in 180s. Packet loss metrics down from 35% -> 3% for those ranges.
Ajay Patel: Running synthetic checks against affected endpoints: 95th latency down from 420ms -> 85ms. DNS lookup success rate back to 99.6% on canaries.
Emily (Customer Success): Sharing update to impacted customers: "We observed intermittent egress disruptions affecting EU-Central due to a transit provider route instability. Traffic has been steered to alternate paths and most customers are seeing restored service. Engineering continues to monitor and is in contact with the provider. We’ll follow up with a post-incident summary." Anything to add?
Maya Chen: Add ETA: continuing monitoring for 60 minutes. If stable, de-escalate to SEV3 and open follow-up with CarrierZ for RCA.
Ajay Patel: Reached out to CarrierZ NOC via peering ticket #CZ-45123; they acknowledged and are seeing packet drops on their internal fabric between POPs. They've queued an engineer and will confirm fix actions.
Sarah Gomez: DNS rollover completed for prod zones to alt-authoritative nodes. No further TTL-related failures observed on canaries.
Leo Anders: Preparing handoff to next oncall (night shift). Tagging @Leo Anders -> next oncall is Leo; handing off all monitoring dashboards and the peering ticket.
Maya Chen: Handoff checklist filled: actions taken, route changes, peering ticket link, customer comms. Leaving follow-up tasks: revert temporary localpref if CarrierZ confirms fix; run post-mortem with RCA in 24h.
PagerDuty Bot: Incident update: SEV2 -> monitoring. Next update scheduled in 15m.
NetOps Bot: Metric summary (after steering): p_loss (CarrierZ egress) 35% -> 2.9%, bpg_flaps 18 -> 2 in 10m window.
Emily (Customer Success): Sent customer update to impacted list and created CS ticket to track replies.
Maya Chen: Thanks team. If anything regresses ping me directly. I’ll leave the channel open and hand off ownership to Leo for overnight monitoring. :thumbsup:
Leo Anders: I’ve taken ownership. Will escalate to CarrierZ if we see any more flaps.
PagerDuty Bot: Incident timeline recorded. Closing note pending final stability check.
